content: {"summary":"fraud-scorer-02 was OOMKilled roughly every 11 minutes after a node rotation placed it on a 32‑core node; the pod ran one gunicorn worker per CPU because WEB_CONCURRENCY was unset, creating twice as many workers as on a 16‑core node and exceeding its 3 GiB memory limit. Setting WEB_CONCURRENCY to 16 reduced the worker count and stopped the OOM loop.","likely_cause":"Default gunicorn worker count (WEB_CONCURRENCY) matched node CPU cores, causing 32 workers on a 32‑core node and memory over‑commit, leading to OOMKilled cycles.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"WEB_CONCURRENCY was unset, so the pod started 32 gunicorn workers on a 32‑core node","evidence_ids":["INC-0163#1"],"quote":"WEB_CONCURRENCY is not set ... starts one gunicorn worker per CPU: 32"},{"text":"The pod was killed after about 20 workers warmed up, matching the 3 GiB limit (~150 MiB per worker) and giving ~11‑minute intervals","evidence_ids":["INC-0163#2"],"quote":"The kill came once about 20 workers had warmed up, which is why each start lasted about 11 minutes"},{"text":"Setting WEB_CONCURRENCY=16 reduced workers and resolved the OOM loop","evidence_ids":["INC-0163#1"],"quote":"WEB_CONCURRENCY=16 set in the Deployment; rollout ... resolved"}],"next_checks":["Confirm that all deployments using gunicorn set WEB_CONCURRENCY explicitly","Monitor per‑worker memory usage after the change to ensure no hidden leaks","Review node pool composition to avoid mixing 16‑ and 32‑core nodes without proper config"]}
